text:
[LNUL.8.10] **Nullable identity/key slot — forbidden.** A `key` / identity slot
must be **non-null**: the compiler refuses a nullable identity slot with
`DS_VALIDATE_NULLABLE_KEY`. Identity relies on **total** equality,
and `null` breaks it — under the `[LNUL.8.2]` split a null key is non-matching
against another null (SQL-style), so a nullable identity silently (a) defeats the
`logical` one-live-per-identity upsert invariant (two null-keyed facts are
distinct identities, never coalesce, and **accumulate without bound**), and (b)
degenerates the identity hash, since every null key hashes to the pinned
`DS_NULL_HASH64` ([LNUL.8.8]) yet compares non-equal — a single-bucket O(N) probe
chain of mutually-non-matching facts, the same bounded-RT / token-budget DoS
`[LNUL.8.2]` exists to forbid, moved onto the identity plane. Key markers are
`logical`-only, so this forbids exactly the meaningless case (a null identity) and
nothing else.

idris.name: Lnul_8_10__same_typed
idris.note: Two non-null values of one type: what a `linear_scan: false` anchor compares, since it pins `key` slots ([LNLS.3.3]) and a `key` slot is never null ([LNUL.8.10]).

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__typed_anchor_decided
idris.note: A NOLINSCAN ANCHOR IS DECIDED: an equality of two non-null values of one type answers true or false, never null and never a trap, so `iret_7_5_1__probe_negated`'s condition holds for every `no` node a `linear_scan: false` program can load.

idris.name: lnls_3_3__negated_anchor_probe
idris.note: A no node probes on its anchor without loss when both anchored slots are non-null and of one type on every candidate. The keyed form gives that premise ([LNUL.8.10]). The singleton form gives it through [LNLS.3.3]'s refusal of an anchor on a nullable singleton slot, which the model does not state, so there the theorem assumes what the clause guarantees.
